## Badge Customization

### Colors
Common badge colors:
- Green: `brightgreen`, `28a745`
- Blue: `0066cc`, `4b32c3`
- Red: `e74c3c`, `ff0000`
- Yellow: `ffd700`, `ffff00`
- Purple: `7b68ee`, `9370db`
- Orange: `ff9800`, `ff8c00`

### Styles
- `flat-square`: Modern, clean look
- `flat`: Default, slightly rounded
- `plastic`: 3D effect
- `social`: GitHub-style stars button

### Examples

Custom color badge:
```markdown
![Custom](https://img.shields.io/badge/Custom-Value-blue?style=flat-square)
```

With logo:
```markdown
![Logo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Powered%20by-Claude%20AI-purple?style=flat-square&logo=openai)
```

## Dynamic Badges

For dynamic/real-time badges, use these services:

### Shields.io
- URL: https://shields.io
- Usage: `https://img.shields.io/badge/{LABEL}-{MESSAGE}-{COLOR}`
- Popular for GitHub stats

### Badgen.net
- URL: https://badgen.net
- Compact alternative to Shields.io

### Codecov
- For test coverage: https://codecov.io

### GitHub Actions
- For CI/CD: Use native GitHub Actions badge

## Testing Badge Integration

1. Copy badge markdown
2. Add to README.md
3. Push to repository
4. Verify badge renders correctly on GitHub
5. Test links work properly

---

## Troubleshooting Badges

**Badge not rendering?**
- Check URL is correctly formatted
- Verify special characters are URL-encoded
- Ensure repo name and username are correct
- Test in a badge previewer: https://shields.io

**Link not working?**
- Verify the target URL exists
- Check GitHub Actions workflows are named correctly
- Ensure release tags follow semantic versioning
